advisories.title: The 'Does not SATISFY' enumeration in Decision item 5 is internally inconsistent in which register rows it names
advisories.observation: Measured against file 08, the thirty slice-affecting V2 rows are DR-101 through DR-130, comprising 4 SATISFIED (DR-102, DR-115, DR-119, DR-123), 2 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED (DR-104, DR-118), 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW (DR-107, DR-122) and 22 OPEN. The draft's list names 23 rows and produces three asymmetries. DR-115 is named although it is already SATISFIED, while DR-102, DR-119 and DR-123, also SATISFIED, are omitted. DR-107 is omitted although it is PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, while DR-122, which carries the identical status, is named. DR-128, DR-129 and DR-130 are omitted although all three are OPEN and every other OPEN row is named.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The enumeration is not the operative scope bound. 'Readiness effect: Zero. Condition 2 stays 4 of 30 SATISFIED' binds all thirty rows at once, and I verified that arithmetic independently against file 08, so no row can move to SATISFIED whether or not it is enumerated. Omission from an illustrative list does not assert the converse. The identical pattern is present in the ADOPTED D-124 record, which likewise omits DR-107, DR-128, DR-129 and DR-130 while naming DR-115, and which both reviewers consented to at 0 MUST-FIX / 0 SHOULD-FIX; charging it here would contradict the adopted precedent that the draft correctly claims to follow. The draft's list is in fact strictly more complete than D-124's, adding DR-104, DR-105 and DR-121.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional and not a condition of adoption. A future recording could either enumerate every non-SATISFIED row or state the bound solely by the condition-2 count and drop the enumeration.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits CONSENT only if there is no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, so the position is CONSENT. Every factual claim the draft makes was re-derived independently: all four measured-input digests reproduce, both verdict files are ACCEPT 0/0 at mode 0444 with the Codex file parsed directly rather than taken on the draft's word, the condition-2 arithmetic of 4 of 30 was recomputed from file 08's Status column and matches, condition 5 is confirmed last and NOT MET, all 26 decisions in the same-form set are ADOPTED with the D-119/D-118 order faithful to COORD, D-125 is correctly distinguished from register row DR-125 with DR-125's recording at D-110 confirmed, the correct file 08 is measured while the decoy is named only to be excluded, and every scope disclaimer required by the dispatch is present and uncontradicted. The three Claude advisories are recorded rather than dropped, which was a named attack. One asymmetry in the item-5 enumeration survives as an advisory; it is not the operative scope bound, which is carried by the verified condition-2 count, and it reproduces a pattern present in the ADOPTED D-124 record that the draft correctly claims to follow.
